articles.title: 'Pathetic': David Warner Makes Blunt Remark Over Poor Crowd At South Africa vs Australia Test
articles.description: David Warner has voiced his frustration over the lack of spectators at the ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia, questioning whether the longest format can truly be considered cricket’s premier contest when stadiums remain largely empty. The former Aussie opener took to his official X account to highlight the disappointing attendance and atmosphere. The ongoing series has therefore sparked debate beyond the results, with crowd attendance emerging as a concern for the future appeal of Test cricket. Warner Questions Test Cricket’s Popularity After Poor Turnout Warner did not hold back in his assessment of the scenes in South Africa, pointing to the contrast between the format’s reputation and the limited number of fans watching from the stands. "We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa? Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving? You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic," The former opener’s post focused on the visible gaps in the crowd and the subdued atmosphere at the venues. Australia’s Durban Victory Fails To Fill The Stands The attendance issue was evident during the opening Test in Durban, where Australia secured a 214-run victory over South Africa at Kingsmead. Despite the significance of the international contest, substantial portions of the stadium were left unoccupied. The sparse turnout has become a talking point because the series features two leading cricket nations. The lack of spectators is particularly notable for South Africa, who entered the contest as reigning ICC World Test Champions. While the quality of competition remains high, Warner’s criticism highlights the importance of building stronger connections between Test cricket and its audience. Consistent support at the ground contributes not only to ticket revenue but also to the atmosphere that makes international sport compelling.

The 19-year-old Sheetal, who equalled the world record and created a new Asian record in the qualification round, defeated Japan's Shinohara Aya 145-137 in the women's compound semifinal to set up a gold-medal clash with Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah. Swati, who is making her Games debut, also assured India of at least a silver medal after beating South Korea's Eunhee Lee 6-2 in the women's W1 semifinal. She will face China's Mengkan in the final. W1 classification is for athletes with significant impairment in functional strength, range of motion, or limb loss across all four limbs. India's recurve and compound mixed teams also advanced to the semifinals with victories over Thailand and Japan, respectively. articles.description: Gianni Infantino's campaign for re-election as FIFA president is set to move this week to Japan and a meeting scheduled for Wednesday with the Asian Football Confederation. articles.title: Shafali Verma reprimanded for breaching ICC Code of Conduct in 2nd T20I
articles.description: India vice-captain Shafali Verma was on Tuesday handed an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe. The 22-year-old was found to have breached Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct during India's nine-wicket victory in Raipur on Sunday. Verma was found to have breached Article 2.2 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to "abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Match," an ICC media release said. In addition to this, one demerit point has been added to Verma's disciplinary record, for whom it was the first offence in a 24-month period. The incident occurred in the 12th over of Zimbabwe's innings when Verma, after dropping Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano at mid-off off Shree Charani's bowling, threw the ball to the ground in frustration.
